transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-04
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Ravi Narayan (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (CTO - SolaceGrid), Marcus Zhao (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security Architect), Aaron Bell (PM)

Summary:
SolaceGrid is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing conversational assistant. Primary goals are: get to first token quickly via PLG/self-serve with free credits, validate latency and cost for 3k-10k daily requests, and confirm security/compliance fit (SOC2, SSO, VPC/KMS). They are undecided between Redwood Hosted API (fastest path) and a Dedicated/Private pilot for data residency and isolation. Action items and a technical deep-dive follow-up were agreed.

Topics covered: quickstart and free credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT) playbook, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem), security/compliance (SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS), perf expectations (95th pct latency targets), pilot scope and timeline, success criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros?
[00:10] Lena: hi, lena here, CTO at SolaceGrid. we'll be leading the evaluation.
[00:15] Marcus: marcus here, i'll be doing the benchmarks and integration work.
[00:20] Priya: priya - security and compliance, i'll vet the audit stuff.
[00:25] Maya: amazing. ethan and i will run through the quickstart and hosting options. rafi is on the thread for CSM stuff - ravi sorry - 
[00:33] Ethan: hi team, i work on inference performance at Redwood, will jump in on latency/cost and pilot design.

[00:45] Aaron: quick note: timeline - we're aiming for a demo to stakeholders in 3 weeks, pilot in 6. is that realistic?
[00:52] Maya: yes that's doable. our PLG path is fastest - sign up, free credits, SDKs — you can get first token in under an hour for simple calls.
[01:04] Marcus: under an hour, ok. what do you mean by free credits and what limitations?
[01:08] Maya: typically we provide a credit pool for new accounts; for pilots we can extend credits sized to expected tokens for two weeks. limitations: rate caps on hosted tier to protect multi-tenant stability, and no private VPC isolation on the hosted credits — for that you move to Dedicated or Private.
[01:26] Priya: for PII and data residency we need the VPC option and the ability to manage keys (KMS/HSM). does Redwood's hosted option support customer-managed keys?
[01:36] Ethan: hosted does encryption at rest and in transit, but CMK/HSM is available on Private deployments; Dedicated has bring-your-own-key options via our enterprise contract. hosted is suitable if data in transit/at rest to Redwood is acceptable and you don't need customer-managed HSM.
[01:53] Lena: ok, so our default plan is: quickstart on hosted to iterate on prompts/user flows, then if things look good we want a Dedicated pilot for isolation and predictable throughput.
[02:02] Maya: makes sense — that's our common pattern. quickstart -> iterate -> pilot -> Dedicated. we can provision a short Dedicated bench if there's a procurement path.

[02:15] Marcus: performance question: our assistant uses 1.2k token context, gen averages 80 tokens, expected 3-10k calls/day. what's realistic latency and cost?
[02:26] Ethan: for that profile on our optimized Llama-family variant you'll see ~60-120ms per token on Dedicated GPU pools (depends on quant + batching). hosted latency SLOs are slightly higher due to multi-tenant queuing but still in the 200-400ms range for end-to-end on that context. cost rough ballpark: hosted per-token is higher than Dedicated reserved. i'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[02:52] Marcus: great. do you do automatic caching or KV cache re-use?
[02:56] Ethan: yes, we have prefix and KV cache mechanisms — sometimes the auto-cacher helps cut cost for repeated prompts; we can enable config for your workload. note transcription sometimes says K V cash on our notes, ha.

[03:12] Aaron: security checklist — SOC2? ISO? SSO? audit logs?
[03:17] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II; we can share the report under NDA. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SSO for admin console. audit logs and token-level observability are in Redwood Console; retention tiers are part of the enterprise package.
[03:36] Priya: good. for the pilot we need an editable retention policy and the ability to export logs for our SIEM.
[03:44] Ethan: that's supported on Dedicated and Private. on hosted we can provide access to logs but the retention windows are fixed unless you purchase extended observability.

[03:58] Lena: what's the friction to getting a quickstart running? our infra team prefers Terraform; are there IaC templates?
[04:06] Maya: yes we have Terraform modules for the Private/AWS deployment and examples for calling the hosted API from any runtime. the SDKs support Python/Node/Java.
[04:15] Marcus: java example would be great, our backend is JVM heavy.
[04:18] Ethan: i'll attach a JVM snippet and a latency benchmark checklist.

[04:28] Aaron: procurement concerns: how long to spin up Dedicated?
[04:32] Maya: Dedicated lead time depends on contract and capacity; for a small pilot we can do a reserved pool in 2-4 weeks after PO, sometimes faster with standard configs. Private (VPC) takes longer due to networking and security review — usually 4-8 weeks.

[04:50] Marcus: any gotchas with model variants / fallbacks? we like having cheaper fallbacks for non-critical queries.
[04:58] Ethan: yes we offer routing policies — you can send lower-criticality traffic to cheaper quantized variants; automatic fallback keeps the app up if the primary is constrained. we'll show routing config in the deep-dive.

[05:12] Priya: data residency: can a Private deployment be hosted in eu-west region? we have eu customers and need EU residency.
[05:19] Maya: Private can be deployed in region of choice; Dedicated has region options but is subject to capacity. hosted data residency options are limited by our hosted region footprint.

[05:28] Lena: ok next: success criteria for pilot. we want 95th pct latency under 800ms, cost per user under $X (we gave a placeholder), and no data leakage — security sign off.
[05:38] Maya: nailed it. we'll map those to measurable metrics and include them in the pilot SOW.

[05:46] Aaron: can we do a small A/B using Redwood's function/tool calling or structured outputs to see if we can improve reranking?
[05:55] Ethan: yes, our streaming responses and function call primitives work well with rerankers. we can set up a canary route to test structured outputs and quality metrics.

[06:06] Marcus: about billing and credits — if we exhaust free credits mid-pilot what happens?
[06:11] Maya: we'll monitor usage; if you hit the cap we'll pause new calls or ask to upgrade. for pilots we typically size credits conservatively and open a billing window for overages.

[06:22] Lena: procurement will want to see a sample contract and SLA.
[06:26] Maya: we'll send the standard pilot agreement and the SLA for Dedicated.

[06:30] Priya: last question - encryption with CMK for Private — is HSM required or optional?
[06:35] Ethan: HSM-backed KMS is optional but available; Customer-managed key support is on Private and Dedicated enterprise tiers.

[06:44] Maya: ok, to recap next steps: i'll email credits/pricing quickstart, ethan will schedule a deeper perf/infra call and attach java snippets and bench checklist, priya will send initial security questionnaire, and we'll target a pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-13.
[07:02] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:06] Marcus: thanks.
[07:08] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
